distinguishing_features: Passive physical vibration suppression rather than prediction of oil-film instability from temperature and speed
A radial spring-mass-damper assembly integrated inside the spindle support structure
Tuning to a selected spindle resonance or critical speed instead of inferring a thermal whirl threshold
Direct reduction of measured resonant vibration amplitude rather than generation of a monitoring indicator
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Reduce vibration amplitude at a selected spindle resonance without materially changing the spindle-bearing interface stiffness or requiring an active control system.
parsed.viable_reason: The specified damper is quantitatively inconsistent with the claimed damping ratio and is far too small to produce the asserted 30% attenuation, while the radial mass also presents unresolved centrifugal-loading and support-isolation issues.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Applying a passive tuned mass damper to suppress a resonance is a textbook mechanical-engineering response, and adapting it radially to a spindle support would be a routine implementation choice.
